page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-1 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the general-purpose tier, built on an arm64 processor architecture. The system provides 1 dedicated virtual CPU coupled with 4.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory allocation. The hardware profile is purely processor-driven, incorporating zero GPUs and providing no bundled local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent disk access relies on attached cloud block storage volumes.

The arm64 architecture necessitates binaries and container images built specifically for 64-bit Arm execution environments. Unlike shared-core or burstable entry configurations, this instance allocates a dedicated vCPU, preventing multi-tenant processor contention and maintaining steady baseline processing capacity. However, with only a single execution core and 4 GB of memory, the configuration does not support highly parallel tasks, memory-intensive caches, or complex compilation runs.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the n4a-standard-1 provides a compact footprint for deployments that do not demand high multi-threaded performance or dense memory allocations. It is appropriate for lightweight microservices, small API gateways, single-process background tasks, basic web serving, and continuous integration testing targeting Arm architectures.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-1 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine utilizing an arm64 processor architecture. It provides 1 dedicated virtual CPU paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated graphics processing units, operating entirely without GPU acceleration, and contains no local storage volumes, requiring external persistent network storage for operational file systems. Lacking specialized hardware acceleration instruction extensions or x86 instruction sets, the platform relies on native 64-bit Arm compilation for executing software stacks. The dedicated vCPU allocation provides predictable, non-burstable processing capabilities suitable for predictable baselines without hyper-threading overhead. Given the modest single-core footprint, the configuration provides efficient resource utilization for low-throughput background tasks, microservices, lightweight development environments, continuous integration test runners, and small web endpoints handling modest traffic.
